neighbours.label: the slot right after seeing or catching someone, where what they are doing comes next (seen me do, catch them in the act), as opposed to other verbs with the same person and to seeing or catching a thing
fire: I've seen him play in Chicago twice now.
We caught her stealing from the till last week.
Have you ever seen them perform at the old theatre?
The teacher caught him cheating on the final exam.
I saw her on stage in Dublin last year.
Police caught the burglar in the act of climbing a fence.
You've seen us work on this all summer.
My mother caught me smoking behind the garage.
quiet: I've seen the film in Chicago twice now.
We gave her money from the till last week.
Have you ever asked them about the old theatre?
The teacher taught him maths for the final exam.
I met her on stage in Dublin last year.
Police followed the burglar in the alley behind a fence.
You've told us about this all summer.
My mother caught the bus behind the garage.

short: slot after seeing or catching someone
notes: Card: ' with' x8, ' act' x5, ' action' x4, ' do', ' live', ' at', after catch or see + person. Probes: 'seen me do' 1.07, 'catch my students being' 0.97, 'catch them in the act' 1.08, 'catch me in' 1.03, 'seen them live' 0.64, 'seen me on' 0.56; 'paid me for' 0.02, 'teach my students about' 0.01, 'told them twice' 0.01, 'reach them in' 0.03; 'met me at' 0.28, and 'caught red-handed' 0.50 with no slot. Peak is often on the word after the person, so the near misses differ on the verb, before it.
